methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $57M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $1.8B.

data.narrative:
Unspun, a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Beth Esponnette, Walden Lam, and Kevin Martin, has raised $57M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 peers—1 public and 8 private—including Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Walden Robotics, spanning the same sector and adjacent stages.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression valuation, using the $57M raised as a proxy for post-money value, applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yielding $114M. Peer-median valuation references three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with a median valuation of $1.6B (range: $1.1B–$1.8B). This method reflects the positioning of later-stage peers such as Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B and Dexterity at $1.6B.

The triangulated range spans $97M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $882M. The wide spread reflects material uncertainty in stage mapping and peer applicability. The stage-progression method anchors conservatively near recent capital; peer multiples suggest substantially higher valuations typical of maturing robotics ventures. Key uncertainties include the degree to which Series B comparables apply to an early Series A, revenue traction not reflected in the data, and the timing between this analysis and the company's next funding event.
